decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to the set square; turn the open gripper toward a downward pinch while preserving elbow-up continuity. Left arm stays at origin.
Advance above the right portion of the ruler while continuing the downward-grasp reorientation, with open fingers and table clearance.
Reduce approach and rotation increments after the continuity rejection; continue above the tool without contact.
Continue small, continuous right-arm motions above the set square; maintain open jaws while rotating downward.
Approach the right-side grasp point from above, keeping the set square and all cubes on the table.
Finish turning the gripper nearly vertical and center it above the right segment of the set square, before descending.
Descend cautiously with vertical open fingers toward the ruler's right segment; use the wrist view to check clearance and centering.
The descent shows likely table contact; ease upward slightly and close around the set square without lifting any blocks.
Test retention with a small table-level slide toward the cubes, while squaring the long edge to a horizontal row; no upward motion.
Pause forward pushing and tighten the pinch; test a small yaw correction with minimal clearance because the tool has not yet followed the intended squaring motion.
Raise only the set-square grasp point a small amount to inspect whether the blade is retained; all cubes remain untouched on the tabletop.
Retention is uncertain in RGB. Reopen and lower for a deeper vertical pinch, removing the yaw test before proceeding with any cube push.
Seat the jaws lower around the thin set square in small increments, then close; stop and re-evaluate if table tracking resistance appears.
Let the deeper pinch settle, then test a short, low sliding correction toward the cubes while monitoring whether the full ruler moves.
The full set square now follows the grasp. Square its edge and slide it toward the nearest cube at constant low height.
Continue the straight, tabletop push so all three cube faces meet the set-square edge and the tilted middle cube turns parallel.
The cubes appear parallel and aligned. Apply a final short seating push, pause, then draw the square back slightly without moving upward near the cubes.
Release the set square on the table beside the aligned row, then raise the empty gripper to begin resetting the right arm.
Back the empty right gripper away from the undisturbed aligned blocks, gaining clearance before the continuous return to its starting pose.
Return the right arm along a gradual elbow-up path, rotating the empty gripper back toward its original orientation. The aligned cubes remain stationary.
Continue the clear return path with small coupled translation and rotation, preserving the current elbow-up branch.
Continue resetting the empty right arm smoothly; keep the left arm stationary and avoid further object contact.
Approach the original right-arm position with decreasing rotation and small translations, staying clear of the completed row.
Slow the final reset approach and correct the left arm's tiny accumulated pose drift toward its original pose; preserve both joint branches.
